limitations: Trustworthiness depends on the task and acceptable risk, neither of which Zitron specifies.

statement.excerpt: LLMs will always hallucinate, their outputs are not trustworthy as a result, they cannot be deterministic, and any chance of any mistakes of any kind are unforgivable.
statement.document_title: I Will Never Respect A Website

from_speaker: their outputs are not trustworthy as a result
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that general-purpose LLMs will retain a propensity to invent false information, not that every answer will be false.
I read 'not trustworthy' as requiring verification before relying on factual answers. The claim supplies no acceptable error rate or application-specific standard.
A finite evaluation with zero observed hallucinations does not establish that a model has no propensity to hallucinate.
criteria.support_condition: A general technical result establishing unavoidable hallucinations across the claimed class, under assumptions that actually cover its ordinary uses, would support the inevitability assertion. Present-day errors alone cannot establish 'always'.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A demonstrated general-purpose LLM with a substantiated guarantee against fabricated factual assertions across its claimed operating scope would contradict inevitability. Zero errors on a limited benchmark alone would not suffice.

evidence.excerpt: Such "hallucinations" persist even in state-of-the-art systems and undermine trust.
evidence.explanation: The paper supports concern about existing systems. Its explanation depends on training and evaluation incentives and does not establish that every future LLM must retain the same problem.

This conditional theoretical result challenges the inference from mathematical inevitability to practical untrustworthiness. It neither demonstrates zero hallucinations in a deployed model nor guarantees that its data assumptions can be met.

The authors report zero hallucinations in an evaluation of 70 academic prompts conducted in February 2025. This is material counterevidence to a claim that hallucinations must occur in every evaluation, but it does not establish elimination of the underlying propensity.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently validated general-purpose model with a substantiated guarantee against fabricated factual assertions, or an impossibility result demonstrably covering the full claimed scope.
